references.text: The blood of the sin offering that is brought into the sanctuary must not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. This is the basis for Moses' argument to Aaron.
The priest who presents the sin offering shall eat it in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
A sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the sanctuary must not be eaten; it shall be burned.
Describes how the blood of the sin offering is to be sprinkled before the veil and applied to the altar of incense, which requires that the meat be burned.
Moses' rebuke of Aaron and his sons for not eating the sin offering in a holy place, which is the context for this verse.
The book of Hebrews refers to this practice: the blood of animals brought into the sanctuary by the high priest as a sin offering results in their meat being burned outside the camp.
